events.body:
## Outcome

Ensure every node computes the same issue, project, review, and thread state from the same signed event set even when events arrive in a different order.

## Implementation

- Specify a total event order using timestamp, event id, and author as deterministic tie-breakers.
- Define duplicate-id handling, authorized tombstone precedence, edit targeting, status conflict behavior, latest review state, and thread resolve/reopen rules.
- Apply the same rules in `IssueStore`, `ProjectStore`, `PullStore`, relay validation, and browser rendering.
- Reject invalid signatures before folding and make replay of an already-seen event idempotent.
- Add shared shuffled-event fixtures consumed by each implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Random permutations of the same fixture always produce identical metadata and rendered state.
- Duplicate and replayed event ids do not change the result.
- Unauthorized tombstones never hide an object.
- Invalid signatures never enter a fold.
- Desktop, relay, and browser fixture results match.

## Dependencies

Depends on #433 so automation and readers share current native fixtures.

## Verification

Add property-style shuffle tests for issues, projects, reviews, inline threads, edits, deletes, status conflicts, and equal-timestamp events.
events.title: Make collaboration-event folding deterministic

events.author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4
events.body:
## Outcome

Ensure every node computes the same collaboration state from the same signed event set, even under concurrent or reordered delivery.

## Implementation

- Specify a total event order using timestamp, event id, and author tie-breakers plus duplicate-id and replay handling.
- Define conflict and tombstone rules for issues, pull requests, comments, labels, reactions, reviews, patchsets, projects, boards, milestones, social objects, moderation actions, and notification cursors.
- Represent concurrent merge, reject, requested-change, waiting, resolve, reopen, and status decisions without discarding independent state.
- Apply the same rules in native stores, relay validation, browser rendering, receipts, and imports.
- Reject invalid signatures before folding and publish shuffled positive and negative fixtures for every object family.

## Acceptance criteria

- Random permutations of the same event set always produce identical metadata and rendered state.
- Duplicate and replayed ids do not change results; conflicting distinct events remain auditable.
- Unauthorized tombstones and moderation actions never hide an object.
- Derived notifications and counts can be rebuilt from the event log and user cursor.
- Desktop, relay, browser, reference verifier, and import folds match.

## Dependencies

Depends on #433 so automation and readers share the native signed format.

## Verification

Run property-style shuffled, duplicated, concurrent, unauthorized, invalid-signature, edit, delete, review, reaction, project, social, moderation, and notification fixtures through every implementation.
